As of 246 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: After the coolest start of the fall season, which saw 
temps ranging from 22F at East Haven, 25F at SLK, and 34F at BTV, 
temps have quickly rebounded into the 50s to lower 60s under gusty 
southerly winds. Peak wind gusts observed have been 41 mph at BTV 
and 51 mph at Colchester Reef so far today.

The core of the strongest 925mb to 850mb jet of 35 to 45 knots will 
be exiting our cwa by 06z, but localized gusts 30 to 40 mph will be 
possible acrs Lake Champlain and exposed ridges thru this evening. 

GOES-19 mid lvl water vapor imagery shows initial s/w energy 
responsible for some lightning north of the eastern Great Lakes 
quickly shearing out to our west. Meanwhile, another potent s/w and 
stronger mid/upper lvl trof is quickly diving southeast toward our 
cwa and should be entering the SLV by 06z. This energy is 
accompanied by a left front quadrant of a 100-120 knot jet at 25h, 
which should help to enhance synoptic scale ascent acrs our region 
for a line of showers btwn 06-12z. Sounding analysis does indicate a 
weak layer of elevated instability with MUCAPE values of 150 to 300 
J/kg, especially over northern NY, so a rumble of thunder is 
possible.  

Meanwhile, additional s/w energy, along with better instability 
develops between 15z and 21z Thursday, supporting additional showers 
with embedded rumbles of thunder possible. The cooling temps aloft 
help to steepen sfc to 3km lapse rates, while MUCAPE values climb 
btwn 800-1200 J/kg. Given the relatively high EQL up to 25kft, a few 
stronger cores wl be capable of small hail/graupel, but probability 
of any severe is <5%. Just not enough confidence in areal coverage 
to mention small hail in grids attm. Highest probability and areal 
coverage of showers on Thurs wl be between 16z and 21z, based on 
moisture/instability and forcing parameters. Given the potential for 
high based showers with favorable deep layer lapse rates, localized 
gusty winds are possible in the stronger cores. Temps under caa 
aloft, warm into the mid 60s valleys to mid/upper 40s summits. 

Mid/upper lvl trof continues to deepen acrs our cwa Thurs night into 
Friday with 925mb to 850mb caa prevailing. This favorable upslope 
flow and lingering 925mb to 700mb moisture wl continue to produce 
plenty of clouds with intervals of showers, especially northern 
Dacks into the central/northern Greens. Highest likely pops wl be 
focused acrs these area, especially on Friday morning. Progged 850mb 
temps drop to near 0C by 12z Friday, so given lingering moisture and 
cooling thermal profiles, a few wet flakes are possible above 3500 
feet in the Dacks and northern Greens from Mt Mansfield to Jay Peak 
on Friday morning. Temps Friday struggle in the mid/upper 30s 
summits to mid/upper 50s warmest valleys.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A 1028mb high pres will be expanding acrs our fa late 
Friday into Saturday with cooler and drier weather anticipated. This 
cool and dry airmass with light bl winds wl allow for temps to 
quickly drop after sunset on Friday night. However, have noted some 
increasing 1000 to 500mb rh after 06z Saturday associated with 
modest waa. This moisture could result in some mid/upper lvl clouds 
toward sunrise on Saturday, preventing temps from completely 
bottoming out. Either way wl mention lows mid 20s to mid/upper 30s, 
very similar to this morning with some clouds increasing over 
northern NY toward sunrise. Saturday is a beautiful fall day with 
temps quickly climbing back into the mid 50s to lower 60s with 
developing southerly winds.

KEY MESSAGE 3: After a stretch of dry and seasonable weather to start 
the weekend, shower chances look to return late Sunday into the 
start of next week. Model guidance at this time shows the remnants 
of current Tropical Storm Isaias will move into the region towards 
the start of the week. At this time, the center of the low looks to 
remain to our south, but widespread precipitation is looking likely 
for Monday into Tuesday. The system will weaken significantly by the 
time it reaches the region, bringing beneficial rainfall. Once this 
system exits, it looks a strong cold front moves through the region 
towards mid-week. As usual with this time range, the trends for 
these systems will need to be monitored as we get closer. 
Temperatures will be on the warm side for Sunday and Monday, with 
highs in the 60s and even low 70s, but will trend cooler for next 
week with highs in the 50s to near 60 for Tuesday.
